item.title: Here's Why NFL Teams Are Making 1 Truly Bewildering Strategy Choice
item.description: When the Carolina Panthers scored a fourth-quarter touchdown to cut Green Bay’s lead to eight points, coach Dave Canales opted to go for 2 instead of kicking an extra point in what has become a far more common decision even if it still bewilders some broadcasters and fans. The Panthers missed and lost by eight last Thursday so the decision proved moot in the end but it’s sure to come up again. Politics: Mike Johnson Fumbles Facts In Denying NFL Game Impact On Convention Viewership So here’s the explanation on why teams have made the switch in strategy. Since the extra point was moved back in 2015, teams have made 94.4% of extra points and 48% of 2-point tries. To do the math, there need to be some assumptions made starting with a team converting at league average rates and overtime being a 50-50 proposition. A team would have about a 45% chance of making the first 2-point try, kicking the extra point and winning in regulation with those numbers, with about a 27% chance of losing in regulation and 28% chance of forcing overtime. That makes for a 59% chance of winning in that scenario. Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost . Rashid Shaheed of the Seattle Seahawks reaches for the ball during a two-point conversion against the Denver Broncos. Justin Edmonds via Getty Images But that doesn’t account for the opposing team being incentivized to be more aggressive if trailing by a point with time left or the specifics of the matchup. The numbers would obviously change if a team is better or worse at making 2-point conversions — Carolina is 2 for 11 in three seasons under Canales — or if overtime isn’t a coin flip. But the broad strokes remain the same. In all, there have been six teams that have faced the choice in the fourth quarter this season, whether to kick an extra point to cut a deficit to seven points or go for 2 and try to make it a six-point game. Four teams went for 2 and two tried for the extra point and they went 0-5-1. The Giants were the only ones that didn’t lose after kicking two extra points after touchdowns to force overtime in a 27-27 tie against Washington in Week 5. item.title: Man United’s Comeback Gives Michael Carrick A Stay Of Execution
item.description: reagan bollig reacts in disbelief after Manchester United misses a goal during a Manchester United FC game viewing at Fred's Around the Corner at 421 Union Ave in downtown Knoxville on Jan. 7, 2025. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect A dramatic 3-2 victory over AS Roma on Tuesday night kept Michael Carrick from losing his job as Manchester United manager. The win was secured by Matheus Cunha, who scored two goals before receiving a second yellow card and being sent off in stoppage time. ESPN reported that the result immediately boosted the 45-year-old’s chances of staying in charge at Old Trafford despite a nine-game winless run. The match looked lost when United trailed 2-0 after just 17 minutes. Carrick’s position seemed hopeless as the team headed for a fifth defeat in six games. A comeback sparked by a re-taken penalty from Bruno Fernandes changed the momentum. On September 10, Cunha netted two goals in the last 10 minutes to give the club its initial victory. The Cost of Survival United held on to win despite playing with 10 men after Cunha’s dismissal. The Brazilian forward celebrated his second goal by jumping into the crowd, which earned him a yellow card from the referee. He then fouled Leonardo Balerdi in stoppage time to receive the second booking that forced him off the pitch. The team managed to survive the final minutes without conceding another goal. This victory ensures Carrick remains the manager for the next game against Aston Villa on Sunday. The club hierarchy hoped the manager would weather the storm of poor results, and this win could mark the start of better times. However, reports from ESPN suggest it would be naïve to view this single result as proof that he must stay in charge long term. Pressure Returns Immediately Next, the squad confronts two difficult Premier League fixtures: first hosting Villa, then traveling to Liverpool. Carrick cannot afford to lose either of these upcoming games or the intense pressure will return. If he loses one of those fixtures, he may be out of a job by December. The turnaround was triggered by a hamstring injury to midfielder Carlos Baleba, which allowed Youri Tielemans to come on as a replacement. This substitution helped spark the remarkable second-half fightback in European competition. The manner of the win will play heavily in the manager’s favor as he navigates the next few weeks of the season. What Comes Next United must now qualify for the Champions League knockout stages to keep the momentum going. The win was crucial for both Carrick and the team’s hopes of advancing in the tournament. The players have high confidence after completing one of the club’s greatest European fightbacks. Mark Ogden and Rob Dawson covered the story for ESPN on November 3, 2026. Although the triumph could prove vital for United’s progression, it instantly strengthened Carrick’s prospects of retaining his position.

item.title: 5 Features That Make Interlagos One of F1's Best Tracks
item.description: Max Verstappen's dominant drive in the wet at the 2024 São Paulo Grand Prix remains one of the greatest drives of his career. (Photo credit: Mark Thompson, Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool) While the modern Formula 1 calendar is stacked with great tracks, fans know that Interlagos is unique in the way that it almost always turns the Brazilian Grand Prix into the most memorable race of any season. But what is it about the track that makes it so incredible? Many fans will be quick to point to Interlagos’ identity as one of F1's classic venues to explain the excitement, and that does play a part. But there are many more reasons why the Brazilian Grand Prix is suited to memorable moments like Max Verstappen ’s greatest drive and Lewis Hamilton 's first championship. Keep reading to find out what those are. Sebastian Vettel's 2012 championship was won on Interlagos’ relentless layout Sebastian Vettel's first-lap spin during the 2012 Brazilian Grand Prix didn't stop him from snatching the championship. (Photo credit: Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool) Interlagos is one of the oldest tracks on the Formula 1 calendar; when it was first opened in 1940, its layout stretched for almost five miles over the rolling countryside between two artificial lakes that provide water to the city of São Paulo. Now, the track is trimmed back to a much more manageable 2.677-mile length, but rather than tarnishing the magic of the original layout, the shorter track has only concentrated the action into a relentless dash that almost guarantees a show for spectators. Part of that comes down to the age of the track. In order for a track to earn the FIA Grade 1 certification that makes it eligible to host F1, modern tracks need to be built to a minimum width and feature ample paved run-off zones. Tracks like Interlagos, which were constructed before those standards came into play, can be ‘grandfathered’ into the calendar. As a result, the track is narrower than many of its contemporaries on the F1 schedule. To make things even more treacherous, Interlagos has very little paved run-off, which means drivers who make a mistake will either hit the grass or a wall. In either case, their race is over. And it was that narrow track that made it so impressive that Sebastian Vettel clinched the 2012 championship at the Brazilian Grand Prix. Coming into the event, Red Bull Racing's Vettel had a 13-point championship advantage over Ferrari's Fernando Alonso , which made him a clear title favorite. Vettel dropped to the rear of the field and reentered the race in 22nd position. item.title: Wilder v Opetaia to serve as co-main for Fury v Joshua
item.description: Deontay Wilder is almost 10 years older than Jai Opetaia [Getty Images] American Deontay Wilder will fight Australia's Jai Opetaia on the undercard of Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua in December. The bout will serve as the co-main event for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight, with the WBA 'super' heavyweight title on the line at Cardiff's Principality Stadium. Unbeaten WBA 'regular' cruiserweight champion Opetaia, 31, will step up to heavyweight for the first time to fight Wilder, a former world champion with 43 knockouts. Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) will hope to re-establish himself among the heavyweight elite, while Opetaia (31-0, 24 KOs) could be eyeing a fresh challenge, after years of dominance at cruiserweight. Wilder, 41, held the WBC heavyweight title from 2015 to 2020 and is regarded as one of the most feared punchers of his generation. The American also enjoyed an epic trilogy with Fury, but came out on the losing side with a draw and two defeats. Wilder had also been close to facing Joshua but a knockout loss against China's Zhilei Zhang in June 2024 derailed the potential bout. Tickets for the main event sold out in under an hour, despite the ringwalks being expected to start around 01:00 GMT on Saturday, 12 December, following a short live music performance, and the stadium will remain open until 03:30. Why is cruiserweight champion Opetaia fighting heavyweight Wilder? This will be a first high-level heavyweight fight for Opetaia, who is a previous holder of the IBF championship and a force at cruiserweight. A move to Zuffa Boxing has brought complications for the Australian - who stopped WBC champion Noel Mikaelian in September but could not claim his belt due to a sanctioning dispute. Opetaia faced off against David Benavidez after his victory over Mikaelian and a future cruiserweight fight could still happen if the Mexican comes through his three-belt unification bout with Michal Cieslak. For Wilder, this presents a chance to be the first professional boxer to get the better of Opetaia. Wilder has lost two of his previous four fights, but picked up a win last time out with a split-decision win over Briton Derek Chisora in April. item.title: Greg Newsome Drops 7-Word Truth After $46 Million Deal
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The most shocking part of Greg Newsome’s new $46 million deal isn’t the cash. It is the seven words he posted right after the ink dried. While the Giants secured a starting cornerback through 2029, Newsome took to X to declare, “BIG BLUE WE ARE HERE TO STAY!!” The 26-year-old is no longer a rental; he is a long-term fixture in a defense that finally looks like a unit. The Money and The Math The financial terms are steep, but the value is clear for a team looking to climb the standings. Fox Sports’ Jordan Schultz reported that the Giants and Newsome agreed to a three-year extension with $32 million guaranteed. That figure represents almost 70 percent of the total deal. The contract raises his average annual value to $15.3 million, which sits right in the middle of the market for top corners. Per reports, this move locks up a key piece of the secondary while the team still has time to make other big moves before the trade deadline. Newsome earned this raise by turning his one-year “prove-it” contract into a career-defining season. He missed the win over Houston due to a concussion, but his stats in the other six games are hard to ignore. When opponents aim at him, quarterbacks have finished only 16 of 29 throws, yielding a 61.4 passer rating. Currently, the Giants hold the third spot in NFL passing defense, surrendering merely 184.9 yards per contest. That is not a fluke; it is the result of a player who finally found the right scheme. Why the Scheme Matters The real story here is how defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson unlocked Newsome’s specific talents. The player himself admitted that his best skill set matches what the Giants ask of him. “With my game, my strong suit I think is playing press man coverage,” Newsome said when he first signed in March. He noted that this style was exactly what he did in Cleveland. Now, he gets to do it every Sunday against the best offenses in the league. This fit is so good that the front office decided to pay up before the season even ended. Newsome spent time with the Browns and Jaguars without finding that same stability. He struggled in Jacksonville, allowing five passing touchdowns in 12 games. The Giants gave him a fresh start, and he rewarded them with zero touchdowns allowed and just two long completions all year. The data shows a player who was simply in the wrong place before arriving in East Rutherford. Securing Newsome changes the math for the rest of the roster. The Giants still have to decide on Deonte Banks, who is entering the final year of his rookie deal. Banks has broken out under Wilson, but now the team knows one half of the tandem is locked in for three years. This stability allows the front office to look at other positions without worrying about the corner spot. The team is 4-2-1 and leading the NFC East, a spot that seemed impossible just a month ago. item.title: Don’t Trade Winn Or Burleson: Cardinals Must Keep Core Intact
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The St. Louis Cardinals are not in a rebuilding mode that requires selling their best young players right now. Patrick McAvoy of Sports Illustrated made the point clear on Wednesday: trading Masyn Winn or Alec Burleson would be a massive error. The team just finished a solid season under Chaim Bloom, winning one fewer game than the year before despite moving veterans like Nolan Arenado and Sonny Gray. The farm system is stocked, and the roster is ready to climb. Selling high on a player like Burleson before he hits free agency makes zero sense when he is the engine of the offense. Winn and Burleson Are The Engine Alec Burleson is one of the most underrated first basemen in the sport. He crushed 26 home runs and led the entire league with 116 RBIs across 160 games in 2026. Masyn Winn had a rough year at the plate, but he was not at full strength for a big chunk of the campaign. Even with the bat struggles, he was elite on the defensive side at shortstop. He is just 24 years old and still has team control. There is no replacement ready to take his spot. JJ Wetherholt could shift positions, which would leave a hole at second base when Jesus Baez is ready to move. Ignore The Noise From Others Bleacher Report’s Zachary Rymer listed both players as top trade assets, but that logic falls apart under scrutiny. Rymer wrote that a contender keeps Burleson, while a rebuilder like the Cardinals should sell high. The Cardinals are no longer a rebuild team. They are a team that took a step in the right direction and needs to keep the pieces that work. In 2027, the young men filling the roster are expected to perform even better. Trading them away now would mean admitting the plan failed before it even started. The front office needs to add around the edges, specifically in the bullpen and back of the rotation, rather than gutting the middle of the lineup. Free Agency Moves Show The Real Path The front office is already making moves that show they value depth over panic trades. On Tuesday, the team announced on X that 10 prospects were declared free agents, including former second‑round pick Tink Hence and left-hander Zack Thompson. They also re-signed three players to minor league deals for 2027, including RHP Randel Clemente, LHP Josh Fleming, and INF Ramon Mendoza. The team is managing roster depth rather than selling assets. The club has work to do, but trading Winn or Burleson is not the answer.

Ohio State lost 30-18. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Ohio State lost to USC by two scores even though the Buckeyes won nearly every statistical category. The real reason for the defeat was a collapse in the red zone. True freshman quarterback Luke Fahey completed just seven of twenty passes inside the forty-yard line. The program now faces its worst stretch since the “Tattoogate” scandal in 2011. Ohio State has dropped four of its last ten games. The last time the team went 6-4 over a ten-game stretch was back in 2011. That year, the program was dealing with the fallout from Jim Tressel’s resignation. Interim coach Luke Fickell led the team to a 6-7 finish before Urban Meyer took over. Meyer soon restored the program to national prominence with a title and a win against “that team up North.” Today, the Buckeyes must adapt their offense to support Fahey if they want to reach the playoff conversation again. The Red Zone Breakdown The box score from the USC game shows a team that dominated but still lost. Ohio State advanced to the red zone on four occasions yet managed to score a single touchdown. The team settled for field goals or failed to score on the other three trips. They finished with just twelve total points in that area. Those missed chances were the main reason for the loss. The offense had eleven drives total. Eight of those drives reached USC territory into what is called the “fringe.” One drive reached the USC 21-yard line and ended in a field goal. Another reached the 31 but ended in a fumble. A third reached the 22 and ended in a field goal. A final drive arrived at the 36 but concluded with a punt following a loss on the play and a five-yard penalty. These stops inside field goal range killed the momentum. This approach lets defenders play aggressively against the run without worrying about deep passes. This also complicates efforts to feature a standout receiver such as Jeremiah Smith. item.description: Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College basketball has never seen anything quite like Olivier Rioux, and the 7-foot-9 giant just proved why. item.description: ANN ARBOR – Maybe there isn’t much buzz nationally and among fans for the Michigan-Michigan State rivalry game this year, but the Michigan players say they are focused and know what’s at stake. First things first for the players, and that’s state bragging rights and the Paul Bunyan Trophy. For Michigan (5-3, 2-3 Big Ten), a win over Michigan State (2-6, 0-5) also would mean bowl eligibility. The teams will play Saturday night, Nov. 7, at Michigan Stadium, and will be streamed on Peacock. “You just think of the history, the magnitude of importance of this game,” Michigan tight end Hogan Hansen said Tuesday night, Nov. 3, after practice. “I think everybody in this building thinks that up until this point, this is our biggest game, state championship, so not very much needs to be said about motivation. Everyone knows what we need to do Saturday night.” This will be the first Michigan-Michigan State game Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham will coach after being hired last December following 21 seasons at Utah. Whittingham said this week he planned to have a few former Michigan players talk to the team about the rivalry. Jon Jansen, a two-time captain who was on the 1997 undefeated AP national championship team, has met with the team. Jansen’s message was clear. “It's going to be a physical-ass game,” Hansen said when asked what Jansen shared. “Be smart, use your head, and just play your tail off.” Tight end Eli Owens said Jansen shared his memories of the rivalry and how much it means for the fans. “At the end of the day, you always want to beat Michigan State, the same way they always want to beat us,” Owens said. “This is a game they have to win, but this is a game that we are going to win. That's just the mindset that we have, and that's the mindset that they have as well. I think that is what makes great football. “I think that when you have two teams that have a rivalry like we have with State, it’s memories and great games. item.title: Eagles Veteran Jalyx Hunt Reveals Locker Room Truth
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Philadelphia Eagles are sitting at 2-6, and the fan base feels like the sky is falling. Yet one veteran player claims the mood inside the building is actually better than it was when the team won the division last season. Jalyx Hunt told 94WIP that the current struggles have united the group in a way the previous year’s success never did. This is a bold take for a team that just lost 27-10 to Washington on Sunday, but Hunt insists the chemistry has shifted for the better. A Strange Shift in the Building Hunt, who has been in the locker room since 2024, admits that winning often hides deep cracks in a team. He told 94WIP, “How it was in the building [last year], it felt a lot worse than this because we were winning, but it felt like we shouldn’t have been winning at times.” That quote cuts deep for fans who remember the 11-6 season and the Super Bowl run. The pressure of maintaining a title while feeling like a fraud can be more toxic than simply trying to fix a broken squad. The difference now is that everyone knows they are not winning, so there is no pretense. According to Heavy.com , Hunt says, “But now we’re just not winning, so everybody’s on the same page in finding an answer, staying positive, and nobody’s quitting.” This unity is real, even if the results on the field remain ugly. The team is last in the NFC East, and the front office has made questionable moves, yet the players say they are all pulling in the same direction. Why Winning Was the Real Problem It sounds counterintuitive to say a losing team has better morale than a winning one, but the evidence from the 2025 season supports it. The Eagles repeated as division champions and won the NFC Championship, yet the locker room felt off. Winning cured nothing because the players knew they were lucky. Now, with injuries piling up and the coaching staff under fire, the honesty is refreshing. However, unity does not fix a defense that allowed 27 points on Sunday. The team needs to stop the bleeding before the next game against the New York Giants on Sunday, Nov. 8. The roster is full of holes, and the coaching staff is struggling to get the right players on the field. Just saying everyone is positive will not stop the Giants from scoring. The Hard Reality of a 2-6 Start While the locker room might be closer, the standings tell a harsh story. The Eagles have not won a game since Week 2, and the season is slipping away fast. Per Yahoo Sports , the defensive line is also dealing with major issues, as Jonathan Greenard has seen very little practice time due to injuries. Vic Fangio noted that Greenard missed training camp and has had “next to none” of the practice reps needed to be effective. A team cannot win with a patchwork defense, no matter how positive the mood is in the meeting room. Hunt’s reveal is a shock to the system, but it might be the most honest thing said all year. The Eagles are in a deep hole, and the only way out is to fix the play on the field.
